1.title: A serious flaw hits some Alpine servers
1.text: A new flaw affects some Alpine Linux servers. An attacker can log in to an account that has no password. The attacker needs the account name and a very long password. The server must allow password logins. OpenSSH has released a fix, version 10.6p2. No attacks have been reported. Admins should update or turn off password logins.

2.title: OpenSSH fixes a login flaw on Alpine Linux
2.text:
OpenSSH released version 10.6p2 to fix a critical flaw on some Alpine Linux servers. Attackers can log in to accounts that have no password, such as accounts that use only SSH keys. They need network access, the name of the account and a password between 257 and 1,024 bytes long.

The server is at risk when it checks passwords without PAM and password logins are on, which is the default on Alpine. At least one other account must have a password. Damien Miller of the OpenSSH project told admins to turn off password logins immediately if they cannot update. No attacks have been reported. Alpine has published fixed packages, but admins must also restart the SSH server after the update.

3.title: OpenSSH issues an emergency fix for a password bypass on Alpine Linux
3.text:
OpenSSH released version 10.6p2 to fix a critical flaw that lets attackers log in to accounts without passwords on some Alpine Linux servers. The attacker needs network access, an account name and a password between 257 and 1,024 bytes long. One account with a real password is enough to expose every account without one. No attacks have been reported.

The problem comes from how sshd works with musl, the C library used by Alpine. When a password is longer than 256 bytes, musl refuses to hash it and returns a star. That star matches the star stored for accounts with no password, so the login succeeds. Servers using PAM or glibc are not affected. A researcher at the firm Wakefield, who reported the flaw, says other musl-based systems such as OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto should be checked.

Alpine published fixed packages for every release back to 3.16. Because upgrading does not restart the running server, admins must restart sshd. Anyone who cannot update can set PasswordAuthentication to no. If a login cannot be ruled out, the advisory says to treat the machine as compromised.
